title: Government-reference-architecture conformance, synthetic-scenario and T&E harness for autonomy and PNT plug-ins (A-GRA, FANTOM Core, UMAA, IOP; pntOS/ASPN and NAVWAR-compliance evidence)
problem: Services now assert government-owned reference architectures for autonomy (A-GRA, FANTOM Core, UMAA, IOP) and PNT (pntOS/ASPN) and require NAVWAR compliance at every milestone, but the conformance toolkits, synthetic-scenario generators and T&E capacity that would let vendors and program offices prove conformance quickly are thin, government-internal or program-by-program, so every integration is re-tested bespoke.

user.exact_role: Autonomy/PNT integration and T&E engineers: (a) at program offices (CCA autonomy evaluation team, SOCOM PEO-SDA UxSAI assessment team, PMS 406 UMAA board, Army PM PNT / C5ISR Center pntOS team, NAVWAR-compliance reviewers under DoDI 4650.08); (b) at vendors who must show conformance (CCA autonomy competitors, SOCOM loitering-munition and mission-autonomy bidders, USV/UUV autonomy vendors, alt-PNT plug-in vendors).
user.echelon: Program office / vendor engineering (not tactical units)
organization_examples: AFLCMC/RCO CCA program office and AFRL autonomy T&E
USSOCOM PEO-SDA / SOFWERX (UxSAI Mission Autonomy Systems Assessment Events)
NAVSEA PMS 406 and the UMAA board (UMAAB)
Army C5ISR Center / PM PNT (pntOS, ASPN, PNTAX/APEX)
Vendors: Shield AI, Collins Aerospace, Anduril, Applied Intuition/EpiSci, small USV/UUV autonomy firms, DIU TQS alt-PNT cohort, TRX, IS4S

current_workflow: Vendor obtains the architecture specification (UMAA ICDs and IDL are public via AUVSI; ASPN-ICD and pntOS-C are public on GitHub since 2026; A-GRA and FANTOM Core interfaces are government-controlled and shared with selected performers only).
Vendor writes its autonomy behaviors or PNT plug-in against the interface using ad hoc, vendor-built simulation and test data (PX4/Gazebo, Unreal, MATLAB, in-house rigs, RF simulators for PNT).

Vendor waits for a government evaluation slot: CCA semi-autonomous flight tests (Feb 2026 onward), SOFWERX/UxSAI assessment events (Aug-Dec 2026), PMS 406 UMAA reviews, PNTAX/APEX field experiment (annual, White Sands).
Government runs limited M&S and field tests; alt-PNT M&S fidelity is lower than GNSS models; issues surface late.
For PNT-using programs, the MDA requires NAVWAR-compliance evidence at each milestone; the evidence package is assembled manually from test reports.
Repeat per vendor and per software drop; each program (air, SOF, maritime, ground, PNT) re-creates its own harness.
current_solution: Vendor in-house simulation (Applied Intuition Axion/Acuity for autonomy; MATLAB/Simulink; PX4/Gazebo; Unreal-based sims), government testbeds (AFRL/AFTC for CCA, SOFWERX assessment events, PMS 406 UMAA board, Army MDQDA/GIANT/CIGNM M&S and PNTAX/APEX), MITRE's low-cost UMAA compliance reference implementation, RTI Connext DDS tooling for UMAA, Spirent/Safran Skydel RF simulators for PNT, and manual NAVWAR-compliance evidence assembly.
failure: There is no shared, architecture-conformant, software-only harness that (1) emits pass/fail conformance reports against the government interface contracts, (2) generates synthetic multi-source scenarios with DDIL/EW and jamming/spoofing conditions, and (3) auto-produces milestone evidence (NAVWAR compliance, safety-case artifacts). Government toolkits were planned (Army pntOS compliance toolkit, GAO 2021) but their release is not publicly evidenced; the M&S fidelity for alternative PNT is 'poorer'; A-GRA and FANTOM Core are not public, so third parties cannot validate a harness without being inside a program.

evidence.claim: GAO reported the Army planned 'a compliance toolkit that can automatically verify that plug-ins for the PNT Operating System comply with its architecture', that alternative-PNT M&S fidelity is poorer than GNSS models, that engagement-level trade tools 'do not yet exist', that field tests need civil airspace closures, and that DoD's MOSA/open-architecture PNT initiative was funded at only $17M FY2020-2024 and may 'peter out'.
evidence.source_title: GAO-21-320SP, Defense Navigation Capabilities: DOD is Developing PNT Technologies to Complement GPS
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: DoDI 4650.08 requires NAVWAR compliance to be determined and reported to the milestone decision authority at each milestone, with T&E plans sufficient to validate it; OPNAVINST 9420.1C requires fleet PNT systems certified as-designed and as-installed.
evidence.source_title: DoDI 4650.08 Positioning, Navigation, and Timing (PNT) and Navigation Warfare (NAVWAR), Change 1
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: In February 2026 the Air Force achieved the first official government validation of the Autonomy Government Reference Architecture (A-GRA), integrating third-party mission autonomy (Collins Sidekick, Shield AI Hivemind) onto both GA-ASI YFQ-42A and Anduril YFQ-44A prototypes; five companies compete on CCA autonomy software, with a downselect expected in 2027.
evidence.source_title: DefenseScoop: Air Force begins testing mission autonomy package for CCA prototypes; FlightGlobal: USAF demonstrates interoperable autonomy architecture across competing CCAs; The Aviationist
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: USSOCOM's June 2026 loitering-munition notice requires the system to support government-owned FANTOM Core collaborative mission autonomy to command the flight controller via an M2M API and/or BMS integration; a separate SOCOM Collaborative Autonomy Integration RFI exists; SOCOM officials said in May 2026 that collaborative-autonomy development is 'not moving fast enough'.
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: SOFWERX and PEO-SDA are running a UxSAI Mission Autonomy Systems Assessment Event series (whitepapers due 2026-09-08; downselects, one-on-one assessments, T&E of selected solutions, final downselect Aug-Dec 2026) for decentralized collaborative autonomy that must integrate into the government's Collaborative Heterogeneous Autonomy Operations Software, and separately a UxSAI Synthetic Data Modeler assessment event (June 2026) for a self-service synthetic-data platform - the government is procuring its own T&E and synthetic-data pipeline rather than a vendor harness.
evidence.source_title: DefenseScoop: SOCOM planning to test new mission autonomy software for unmanned systems program; Soldier Systems Daily; sam.gov UxSAI Synthetic Data Modeler AE
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: UMAA 6.0 (Dec 2023) ships a Compliance Specification with ICDs/IDL; MITRE publishes a 'low-cost solution for UMAA compliance' (a reference implementation for small USVs); RTI presented adapting MOOS-IvP to UMAA (MOOS-DAWG 2024); a small firm (Weathergage Tech) markets 'UMAA compliance with far less effort'; PMS 406 posted a UMAA-compliant software solicitation in 2023 - several partial, mostly free or government-funded compliance aids exist for the maritime architecture.
evidence.source_title: MITRE: A Low-Cost Solution for the U.S. Navy's UMAA Compliance; AUVSI UMAA ICDs; RTI MOOS-DAWG 2024 paper; sam.gov UMAA compliant software
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: Navy SBIR 26.5 open topic DON26BX05-NP004 (NAVWAR, GPNTS transition owner) accepts synthetic ASPN/pntOS data for Phase I and states 'innovation required on the ingestion of disparate types of APNT data sources and how to standardize those types of data' - i.e., a synthetic ASPN scenario source is a recognized need.
evidence.source_title: Navy SBIR DON26BX05-NP004 topic and Q&A
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: pntOS-C and the ASPN-ICD (ASPN 2023, 53 sensor message definitions) are public; in 2026 ISTO announced the PNT Standards Consortium founded by Leidos, IS4S and TRX Systems to govern pntOS and ASPN and 'simplify the use of standards to encourage implementation' - the standards are open but no public conformance test suite is evidenced.
evidence.source_title: ISTO announces formation of PNT Standards Consortium; pntstandards.org; Open-PNT/pntOS-C GitHub
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: PNTAX (sixth annual, hosted by AFC All-Domain Sensing CFT at White Sands) was to be renamed the All-domain Persistent Experiment (APEX) from FY25 Q4 with an expanded scope (sensor/comms architectures, data transport, edge processing under a realistic threat environment) - the government's own field-assessment venue for PNT/autonomy remains an annual, capacity-limited event.
evidence.source_title: army.mil: Sixth annual PNT Assessment Experiment aligns Army priorities, capabilities
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: GAO-25-106931: only 14 of 20 reviewed programs implemented MOSA to some extent, none analyzed MOSA costs and benefits, and a GAO official said in June 2026 that MOSA implementation is still lagging - the policy driver for conformance tooling is real but weakly enforced.
evidence.source_title: GAO-25-106931 Weapon Systems Acquisition: DOD Needs Better Planning to Attain Benefits of Modular Open Systems
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: CCA Increment 1 FY2027 request is reported at about $2.5B (about $1B procurement), up from $891M enacted in FY2026; autonomy T&E is funded inside the program, not as a standalone line.
evidence.source_title: Shephard CCA programme page; Air & Space Forces Magazine: Air Force wants nearly $1 billion to start buying CCAs in 2027
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: Applied Intuition markets Axion as an end-to-end autonomy platform that 'unifies developers and operators in a shared digital environment, accelerating testing, integration, and deployment across all domains' and acquired EpiSci (Jan 2025); this is company marketing, not proof of A-GRA/UMAA conformance tooling, but it shows the best-funded adjacent vendor is aiming at the same T&E/integration slot.
evidence.source_title: Applied Intuition press: Axion and Acuity; Applied Intuition acquires EpiSci
evidence.label: FACT

why_existing_startups_havent_solved: Three structural reasons. (1) Access: A-GRA and FANTOM Core are government-owned and only shared with selected performers; the full government ASPN message set requires citizenship/contractor verification; only UMAA and the public ASPN/pntOS-C subsets are open, so an outsider cannot validate a harness against the architectures that matter most. (2) The government is building the tooling itself: the Army planned an automatic pntOS plug-in compliance toolkit (GAO 2021), MITRE publishes a UMAA compliance reference implementation, and SOCOM is procuring its own UxSAI assessment events and synthetic-data modeler - free or government-funded substitutes suppress a paid market. (3) Small, fragmented customer base: a few dozen autonomy and alt-PNT vendors plus five program offices each owning a different architecture; T&E money sits inside programs (CCA, PMS 406, PM PNT) rather than in a standalone line, so nobody has a budget object called 'conformance harness'. Applied Intuition (well funded, EpiSci lineage) is the closest commercial player and has so far sold platform-level simulation rather than architecture-specific conformance.
technical_wedge: Narrow to the open sub-problem: a software-only 'PNT and autonomy interface digital twin' that (a) generates synthetic ASPN 2023 measurement streams (GNSS, IMU, clock, magnetic, vision, RF-ranging) and multi-vehicle mission-message traffic under scripted degradation (jamming, spoofing, link loss, latency) using public schemas (ASPN-ICD YAML, pntOS-C API, UMAA IDL, MAVLink/STANAG 4586); (b) runs a vendor's plug-in or autonomy container against those streams in CI and scores schema conformance, behavioral conformance (DHS Resilient PNT Conformance Framework levels 0-4, UMAA compliance specification) and mission-outcome metrics; and (c) exports a structured evidence package mapped to DoDI 4650.08 NAVWAR-compliance questions and MOSA planning elements. Sell first to vendors preparing for PNTAX/APEX, SOFWERX UxSAI and PMS 406 reviews; later license to program offices as the shared harness. Restricted architectures (A-GRA, FANTOM Core) are added only inside a government-sponsored effort with cleared US-person staff.

mvp.what: Open-core CLI/CI harness: ASPN synthetic scenario generator + pntOS-C plug-in conformance suite + UMAA/MAVLink message-contract checker, with a hosted report that renders DHS-CF resilience level and a draft NAVWAR-compliance evidence table.
mvp.demonstrable_in_3_6_months: Run a public pntOS-C example plug-in and an open-source USV/UAV autonomy stack (MOOS-IvP or PX4) through 20+ scripted degradation scenarios (TEXBAT-class spoofing, jamming ramps, link dropouts) and publish pass/fail conformance reports and resilience-level scoring; show a 20-vehicle Gazebo scenario with link-loss injection and automated UMAA/MAVLink contract checks.
mvp.what_it_must_prove: That schema-plus-behavior conformance findings from the harness predict real integration failures (validated with at least two vendors' plug-ins under NDA), that the synthetic ASPN streams are accepted as Phase I evidence by NAVWAR/PM PNT reviewers, and that a vendor will pay (pilot fee) rather than wait for the government's free toolkit.

data_requirement.what: Interface specifications (ASPN-ICD, pntOS-C API, UMAA ICDs/IDL, MAVLink, STANAG 4586 public parts), open navigation datasets for scenario grounding, public spoofing/jamming test datasets, and (later) government threat conditions and restricted architecture documents.
data_requirement.legally_realistically_obtainable: Yes for the open subset: ASPN-ICD and pntOS-C are Distribution A on GitHub; UMAA ICDs are public via AUVSI; DHS Resilient PNT Conformance Framework, PNT Integrity Library and NIST IR 8323r1 are public; MagNav open flight data (DAF-MIT) and TEXBAT spoofing datasets are public. No for the government ASPN message set (citizenship/contractor verification), JNWC threat conditions (CUI/classified), A-GRA and FANTOM Core interface documents (government-controlled, program access only).

entry_vehicle.eligibility_notes: SBIR requires >50% ownership and control by US citizens or permanent residents (13 CFR 121.702); the Indonesian founder's shares never count and the German founder's count only after the green card. AFWERX open topics limit foreign-national participation to public-domain/fundamental research and require work in the US. DoD SBIR proposals require foreign-national identification and export-control compliance. B2B sales to vendors carry none of these barriers, which is why the vendor-first sequence is proposed. Needs counsel: SBIR ownership, ITAR status of autonomy-interface work, deemed-export controls for the Indonesian founder.

incumbent_response.could_anduril_palantir_l3harris_add_it: Yes, easily for their own stacks: Anduril (Lattice simulation), Shield AI and Collins already run in-house A-GRA test rigs as CCA autonomy competitors; Applied Intuition can extend Axion; primes and FFRDCs (MITRE) can publish free reference implementations; the ISTO consortium or C5ISR Center can release an official pntOS conformance suite that resets the market to zero price.
incumbent_response.why_startup_still_wins_or_reject: A startup wins only if it is the vendor-neutral, open-core arbiter that program offices prefer over any competitor's rig (a competitor cannot credibly grade its rivals), and if it moves first on the open ASPN/pntOS/UMAA subset before the consortium ships an official suite. Reject if the government publishes its toolkit or Applied Intuition bundles conformance scoring for free; both are plausible within 12-24 months. Net: defensibility is weak; the win case depends on speed and neutrality, not technology.

regulatory_burden.explanation: The open ASPN/pntOS/UMAA/DHS-CF subset is Distribution A or public and can be built as EAR99-style commercial software; but the moment the product ingests military autonomy interfaces (A-GRA, FANTOM Core), JNWC threat conditions or real NAVWAR test data it becomes CUI/ITAR-adjacent (USML Cat VIII(h)/XI(d) technical data is likely for military UAS autonomy - INFERENCE, needs counsel). Government use requires DFARS 252.204-7012/NIST SP 800-171 and CMMC self-assessment, IL4/IL5 hosting and probably Iron Bank hardening. No clearances are needed for the vendor-pilot phase.
regulatory_burden.non_us_person_founder_note: The Indonesian founder can work on the open, public-standard core; must be walled off (technology control plan, possibly BIS deemed-export licence or DDTC TAA - counsel required) from any ITAR/600-series technical data such as restricted autonomy interfaces or government ASPN message sets that require citizenship verification. The German founder's constraints ease at permanent residence (ITAR treats an LPR as a US person, 22 CFR 120.62). SBIR eligibility requires the post-PR German founder plus US-citizen/PR holders to exceed 50% ownership and control.

dual_use_potential.explanation: The PNT half has a civil twin: DHS Resilient PNT Conformance Framework, NIST IR 8323r1 and EO 13905 push critical-infrastructure operators (telecom timing, aviation, maritime, power) toward resilient-PNT conformance, and DOT/DHS complementary-PNT programs need scenario-based testing. The autonomy half (UMAA/MAVLink contract testing, multi-vehicle DDIL scenarios) maps to commercial USV/UAV fleet operators and drone-delivery certification but that market is nascent. Military reference-architecture conformance itself has no civil buyer.

defensibility.explanation: Proprietary value would be the library of scenario packs and degradation models, per-architecture conformance rules validated against real program findings, an accredited (IL4/IL5, Iron Bank) hosted evidence service, and a neutral-arbiter reputation with program offices. None of this is a strong moat: the standards are open, the government can publish free suites, and simulation incumbents can replicate the models. Network effects are weak because the vendor population is small.

why_now: Between 2025 and 2026 the government-owned-architecture model went from policy to practice: A-GRA received its first official validation with five autonomy competitors on two CCA airframes (Feb 2026); SOCOM mandated FANTOM Core integration in solicitations (Jun 2026) and stood up UxSAI assessment events with T&E phases (Aug-Dec 2026); UMAA 6.0 added a compliance specification (Dec 2023) and ICDs are public; ASPN-ICD (Jan 2026) and pntOS-C (Apr 2026) became public and the ISTO PNT Standards Consortium formed (2026); NAVWAR accepts synthetic ASPN/pntOS data as SBIR evidence (Aug 2026); GAO (Jan 2025, Jun 2026) keeps pressing MOSA enforcement. Simultaneously the vendor population that must prove conformance grew (CCA autonomy competitors, DIU TQS alt-PNT cohort, LEO-PNT, SOCOM munition bidders).
killer_risk: The buyers are the builders: the Army planned its own pntOS compliance toolkit, MITRE already publishes a free UMAA compliance reference, and SOCOM is procuring its own assessment events and synthetic-data modeler - so the paid market is a few dozen vendors buying a stopgap until free government or consortium tooling arrives, while the highest-value architectures (A-GRA, FANTOM Core) are inaccessible to an outsider and ITAR-adjacent, and Applied Intuition can bundle conformance scoring into Axion at any time.

allied_extension: Somewhat more compelling for the PNT half and less for the autonomy half. Allies face the same GNSS-denial problem and NATO/AUKUS navies are converging on UMAA/STANAG 4586-style uncrewed C2 interfaces (AUKUS Maritime Big Play 2025), so an open ASPN/UMAA conformance harness could serve UK, Australian and German vendors; the ISTO consortium is industry-governed, not US-government-restricted. But A-GRA and FANTOM Core are US-only, allied autonomy stacks (Helsing, ARX, Quantum Systems) are closed vertical stacks, and exporting or servicing a harness for a foreign military may constitute an ITAR defense service (needs counsel). A German-domiciled entity would be NATO Innovation Fund-eligible but would then face US-side FOCI/ITAR friction for the US program-office sale.
